headers._comment: Both patterns are needed. Firebase matches the REQUEST path, not the file it resolves to, so a rule on /index.html alone never fires for a browser asking for / - which is every visitor. That left the root page on Firebase's default one-hour cache while every other asset was fresh, so a deploy appeared not to land.

no-cache means revalidate, not 'do not store': the CDN still serves a fast 304 when nothing changed. These files are ~10KB, so a real max-age buys almost nothing and costs a stale build at the worst moment - push a fix on demo day and the edge serves the old one.
